reference.title: Dumbbell Seated Neutral Wrist Curl
reference.listing: Page could not be read (gymvisual.com blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Exhale as the hands curl up, inhale as they lower.
breathing.cadence: About 1 s up, 0.4 s squeeze, 1.7 s down

prescription.load: Dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control through the full range for every rep with 1-3 reps in reserve (RPE 7-9). Wrist curls need a light dumbbell.
prescription.progression: More reps, then a slower lowering, then a heavier dumbbell (small steps)

cues.text: Sit on the end of the bench, feet flat, forearms along the thighs with the thumbs up and the wrists just past the knees; let the dumbbells tip the hands down.
Breathe out and cock the hands up toward the thumbs, bending only at the wrists.
Hold the top briefly; the forearms stay on the thighs.
Breathe in and lower slowly until the hands tip down toward the little-finger side.
Keep a firm grip at the bottom; repeat.

mistakes.fix: Keep the forearms pinned to the thighs; only the hands move.
Lower slowly and pause before curling.
Keep the thumb pointing up the whole time; only the hand tilts.
Lean forward from the hips with a long back.

kinematics.norm: Healthy adults used up to about 17 degrees of radial and 40 degrees of ulnar deviation in daily tasks, functional range about 10 radial and 30 ulnar (Ryu 1991); a curl moves through a comfortable range without pain (clinical opinion)
Forearms rest along the thighs and stay still; only the hands move, the wrists just past the knees so the hands move freely (clinical opinion)
Lean forward from the hips with a long back so the forearms lie flat on the thighs (clinical opinion)

Slow and controlled, about 1 s up, a short squeeze and 1.5-2 s down (clinical opinion); resistance programmes for the wrist extensors in tendinopathy used 1-4 sets of about 15 reps, with no optimal dose defined (J Hand Ther 2012)

sources.title: GymVisual Dumbbell Seated Neutral Wrist Curl, video page (movement reference; page not readable here)
Ryu, Cooney, Askew, An and Chao 1991, functional ranges of motion of the wrist joint (J Hand Surg Am 16(3):409-419; 40 adults, biaxial wrist electrogoniometer)
Szymanski, Szymanski, Molloy and Pascoe 2004, effect of 12 weeks of wrist and forearm training on high school baseball players (J Strength Cond Res 18(3):432-440; PubMed 15320673; 43 players)
Effectiveness of different methods of resistance exercises in lateral epicondylosis, a systematic review (J Hand Ther 2012;25(1):5-25; PubMed 22075055; 12 studies)

cautions: Thumb-side wrist pain (for example at the base of the thumb): shorten the range and use a lighter dumbbell (clinical opinion).
Wrist or elbow pain: use a lighter dumbbell and a shorter range; stop if pain persists (clinical opinion).
Keep the forearm on the thigh so the elbow and shoulder stay out of it.
Stop if sharp pain, numbness or tingling occurs.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Forearms on a flat bench instead of the thighs (kneeling beside it).
One arm at a time to focus on control.
regressions: Hold the dumbbell nearer the top plate.
progressions: Hold the dumbbell by the far end of the handle (longer lever).

muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_r: The radial wrist extensors (extensor carpi radialis longus and brevis) with flexor carpi radialis cock the hand up toward the thumb side (radial deviation) (clinical anatomy).
muscleNotes.forearm_extensors_l: The radial wrist extensors (extensor carpi radialis longus and brevis) with flexor carpi radialis cock the hand up toward the thumb side (radial deviation) (clinical anatomy).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_r: Flexor carpi radialis helps lift the hand toward the thumb side; the finger flexors hold the handle and flexor carpi ulnaris controls the lowering (clinical anatomy).
muscleNotes.forearm_flexors_l: Flexor carpi radialis helps lift the hand toward the thumb side; the finger flexors hold the handle and flexor carpi ulnaris controls the lowering (clinical anatomy).
muscleNotes.biceps_r: Holds the elbow bent while the forearm rests (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.biceps_l: Holds the elbow bent while the forearm rests (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Holds the forward lean with a long back.

phases.label: Wrists bent back, forearms on the thighs

guides.label: Hand cocks up toward the thumb side
